title: Team Collaboration with a colleague
npc_personality: neutral, Neutral and businesslike; matched to a challenging teaching tone at slow pacing, wants to Protect their own priorities in the team collaboration situation and Be seen as reasonable by anyone who hears about this later
context: The learner and their colleague, Alex, are meeting in the conference room after a sprint review. A recent project deadline was moved up, causing the team to scramble and reassign tasks. Alex, who manages the resource allocation, is neutral but firm, and wants to understand the learner's rationale while protecting their own priorities.
opening_npc_line: Hey, I noticed the client deliverable timeline was shifted last minute, and the team had to reallocate resources—can you explain why that decision was made without consulting us first?

required_beats: The counterpart states their position on the team collaboration issue, giving the learner something concrete to respond to
The learner is given a clear opening to state their own position
An opportunity for the learner to acknowledge the counterpart's constraint before pressing their own
A moment requiring the learner to restate something complex clearly and concisely
The counterpart applies pressure that the learner must hold their ground against at least once
plan_generated.hidden_concern: They are under pressure themselves and have less room to move than they are willing to admit up front
likely_objections: The learner's concern is real but not the most urgent thing right now
Someone above them has already committed to the current course
This has been handled the same way before without complaint
failure_modes: Learner agrees to everything to end the discomfort
Learner never states a position, only asks questions
Learner becomes combative and attacks the counterpart personally
Learner leaves with no concrete next step agreed
formative_checkpoints: After the opening exchange: did the learner state a position or only react?
Mid-conversation: is the learner exercising trust building or avoiding it?
At the pressure beat: did the learner hold, fold, or escalate?
At close: is there a concrete, mutually understood next step?
